summary:
Bermuda is a British Overseas Territory. The United Kingdom's Equality Act 2010 and its 2025 single-sex services code do not automatically extend to Bermuda. Local legislation governs, and United Kingdom measures could be applied to Bermuda only by Order in Council.

The House of Assembly voted 22–16 on 14 May 1994 to decriminalise consensual sex between adult men, striking two sections of the Criminal Code. The debate divided the island at the time, with religious leaders split and the Christian Coalition staging marches against the change.

In July 2013 the Senate passed the Human Rights Amendment Act, which outlawed discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation and, in the same instrument, on grounds of age. Same-sex marriage was not permitted at that point.

The Governor gave assent to the Domestic Partnership Act in February 2018. It replaced same-sex marriage with domestic partnerships open to both same-sex and opposite-sex couples, making Bermuda the first jurisdiction to revoke marriage equality. Partner recognition for a same-sex couple therefore rests on the partnership register rather than on marriage.
tangentialFactors:
Organised religious hostility toward visible same-sex couples has been demonstrated publicly. The AME church in Bermuda and other churches protested a cruise ship carrying gay passengers, condemning the visit as incompatible with the word of God and the Christian moral fibre. Hostility in Bermuda has been mobilised around the visible presence of same-sex couples, including visitors arriving by ship, not only around local conduct.

Religious opposition has repeatedly entered the public record: churches marched against the 1994 decriminalisation vote, and religious bodies campaigned in the period leading up to the 2018 Act. A same-sex couple should expect public objection to be expressed openly rather than confined to private opinion.

Partner recognition has proved reversible here. Bermuda moved from permitting same-sex marriage to prohibiting it in 2018, so marital status should not be assumed to travel with the couple. Opposite-sex marriage remained unaffected by the Act.
localsOnly:
Residents are protected from discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation under the human-rights legislation as amended in July 2013, and the same amendment added age to the prohibited grounds.

Residents of any sex may register a domestic partnership, which is the relationship status available to both same-sex and opposite-sex couples since 2018.
outOfScopeNotes:
No source in this inventory addresses gender recognition, legal gender markers on passports or local identity documents, entry or visa screening that could disclose gender history, or any criminal, civil or health provision referring to gender identity as distinct from sexual orientation. A trans visitor's specific exposure cannot be determined from these sources.

Whether the United Kingdom's 2025 single-sex services code has been applied to Bermuda by Order in Council is unresolved here; no instrument extending it is cited, and the sources describe the position as one in which local legislation governs.

The cruise-ship protest reported by PinkNews is dated only to 12 July, with no year given in the source, so the event cannot be placed precisely on the timeline.

Hate-crime provisions, police recording of offences against trans people, and any restriction on gender-affirming care are not sourced in this inventory.
